scope: Send Patch MIME serialization foundation; no native composition or delivery acceptance

checks.independent_parser: Python standard-library email BytesParser with policy.default
cases: All four source preparation modes retain distinct To/CC, Unicode display names, exact bodies and ordered attachment snapshots
Long Unicode subjects and RFC 2231 filename continuations, including quotes/semicolon/newline and long multibyte names
Opaque encoded subjects decode once; long multiword encoded subjects fold without double encoding
All 256 byte values survive binary attachment decoding without reading original path
Empty body/recipients and unique IDs; explicit UTF-8/Latin-1 body charset without byte rewriting
Header injection/control bytes, invalid mailbox syntax, nonfinite dates, oversized header tokens rejected
Encoded fields enforce 76-character lines; general message lines bounded to 998 bytes
Real binary patch series serialized as separate inline MIME messages applies with both Git engines to identical tree; source HEAD/index unchanged
checks.initial_review_fix: Reduced encoded word chunks and folded display-name/address lines after RFC 2047 field-width review; final tests/builds rerun
checks.side_effects: No main app or mail client launched; no drafts, network sends or preference suites created

limitations: MIME builder is not yet wired to app consumers; native Send Patch dialog, checked list and all caller routing pending
Git-config sender identity, mail-client/SMTP backend, envelope validation, TLS/authentication/Keychain, progress/retries/cancellation pending
Broader charsets, SMTPUTF8, address groups/comments, mixed raw-Unicode/encoded-word subjects, unfoldable long encoded fields and large-message streaming require acceptance
Payload bytes are retained rather than upstream 8bit text CRLF normalization; parser and Git am checks cover current scope only
Actual signed AppStore sandbox/Finder/distribution and physical UI acceptance pending; hosted GitHub CI unverified
